requestedActions.title: Read titles of work packages the connected person can access, including paginated results

prohibitions: Creating, updating, or deleting work packages
guide.summary: OpenProject documents OAuth applications with Authorization Code and Client Credentials flows. The OAuth app must be created by an administrator in the instance, and scopes are selected there; if no scope is checked, api_v3 is assumed. The read action maps to the work package collection endpoint with offset-based pagination, but the exact permission identifier needed to read work packages is not named in the supplied snapshots, so coverage is unresolved. Customer instances must each register or connect their own OAuth application with the user-supplied base URL.

findings.title: Authorization Code flow with client ID, secret and redirect URI
findings.detail: OpenProject documents an authorization code flow using the instance Auth URL and Access Token URL, with a configured redirect URI, client ID and client secret obtained after creating the OAuth application.
findings.appliesWhen: Connected customer acts as their own user on the customer instance.

findings.title: Each customer instance must register its own OAuth application
findings.detail: The OAuth application is created under Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications on the instance, which requires an administrator with the application-level permission to create an OAuth app.
findings.appliesWhen: Every customer organization or workspace connects to its own OpenProject instance.

evidence.quote: OAuth applications To configure OpenProject to act as a server to an OAuth client application, please navigate to Administration -> Authentication -> OAuth applications .
- Create and configure an OAuth app
To add a new OAuth application, click the green + OAuth application button.

findings.title: api_v3 scope is the standard OpenProject API scope
findings.detail: If no scope is checked, api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope and is the documented default for OAuth applications.
findings.appliesWhen: Developer-owned OAuth requests the standard API for work package reads.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.
"scope" : "api_v3" ,

steps.title: Register developer-owned OAuth application on each customer instance
steps.detail: On each customer OpenProject instance, an administrator creates an OAuth application under Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications, selects the api_v3 scope, sets the redirect URL, and stores the Client ID and Client secret. No registration is claimed as completed by this step.
steps.doneWhen: The customer admin has created the OAuth application and recorded its Client ID, Client secret, and redirect URI for the developer's use.

evidence.quote: Add a new authentication application for OAuth
To add a new OAuth application, click the green + OAuth application button.
Tip Don’t forget to note down your Client ID and your Client secret in a safe space. You will need them later.

fields: <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>: customer's own HTTPS OpenProject base URL, user-supplied
Client ID and Client secret: values copied from the OAuth application
Redirect URI: must match the value configured in the application

steps.title: Obtain user-scoped access token via authorization code flow
steps.detail: The connected person authorizes the developer app at the instance Auth URL with scope api_v3. The developer's server exchanges the returned authorization code at the instance Access Token URL. This step does not claim consent was given or a token was issued.
steps.doneWhen: A Bearer access_token with scope api_v3 is returned by the token endpoint for the connected person.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
--data 'redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>' The response will look like this:
The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.

fields: Auth URL: <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>/oauth/authorize, built from the customer base URL
Authorization code: returned to the redirect URI after the connected person consents
Client credentials flow is not used because it acts as the app, not the person

steps.title: Read first page of accessible work package titles
steps.detail: Lists work packages visible to the connected person with offset pagination. Titles come from the subject property of each element in _embedded.elements. Expected success is HTTP 200 with a collection object containing total, count, pageSize, and offset. Permission needed to view work packages is unresolved in the snapshots.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 returns a collection where each element subject is read, and the response includes total, count, pageSize, offset, and _links.nextByOffset when more pages exist. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.
Parameters offset integer optional query
offset The page number that is requested from paginated collection Integer when offset based available

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
<ACCESS_TOKEN>: access_token from the token exchange step
filters=%5B%5D: empty filter array so no default filter is applied
offset=1 and pageSize=5: documented query parameters for the first page

steps.title: Read next page of accessible work package titles using returned next link
steps.detail: Repeat the same read using the next link returned by the prior response at _links.nextByOffset. Resolve a relative href against the HTTPS instance base URL. Keep the same parameters and token. Repeat while the response includes a nextByOffset link; stop when no nextByOffset link is returned.
steps.doneWhen: Each response's subjects are collected, and iteration stops when a response has no _links.nextByOffset link. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: nextByOffset Link to retrieve the following page of elements (offset based) when offset based available
pageSize Amount of elements that a response will hold Integer when paginated
get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.

fields: <NEXT_PAGE_URL>: value of _links.nextByOffset.href from the prior response
Relative href resolves against the HTTPS <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>
<ACCESS_TOKEN>: same access token as the first request

unknowns: The specific permission needed to list accessible work packages via GET /api/v3/work_packages is not stated in the supplied snapshots.
Whether the api_v3 scope alone is sufficient for the read action is not explicitly documented.
Client Credentials flow is documented but is an app actor, not a per-user token, so it is not suitable for reading as the connected person.
